summary: Washington DNR live-in fire tower on Sekiu Mountain, Clallam County: built 1964, in service June 1965, removed or destroyed 1988. Nothing on the summit is described today.

facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1988; no source describes what remains on the summit

access.note: The route is on gated Olympic Tree Farm land that WillhiteWeb describes as open to recreational use

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb gives 2.6 miles and 1,600 feet of elevation gain, by good gravel road to the summit

events.note: Register, Rex's page and WillhiteWeb give 1964; a DNR report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 1962-64
Mrs. Della Turner, wife of the DNR fire warden, was the first to live in the tower after DNR put it into operation on June 15
Sekiu Mountain listed as one of three lookouts to be manned, per a Port Angeles Evening News item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Mike Drovdahl worked a summer in the lookout
Register says removed; Rex's page says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says removed or destroyed

corrections.why: The register and WillhiteWeb both describe a 40-foot tower (about 12.2 m); 292.6 does not fit a tower of that size

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, Rex's page and WillhiteWeb say 1964; a DNR report quoted on Forest Lookouts says erected 1962-64; an April 1964 item called it new and still to be built; DNR put it into operation June 15, 1965
Register gives 1,943 ft (592 m); the 1965 newspaper item quoted by WillhiteWeb gives 1,960 feet for the mountain. The record's 592.2 follows the register
Register says removed in 1988; Rex's page says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says removed or destroyed. The record's gone status stands

notes_for_editor: Build year and in-service date differ (1964 vs June 1965). The destruction account comes from WillhiteWeb alone, which says a similar story is told for Mount Octopus. No source describes the summit today. Record height_m 292.6 does not fit a 40-foot tower. Access level restricted reflects the gate. Staffing as_of 1988 is inferred from the removal date.
